extracted.intended_audience: patent searchers, chemical indexers, and patent information professionals using Derwent DWPI/CPI
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for assigning and searching Derwent Chemical Codes in patent records (DWPI/CPI), including code selection, subheadings, time-ranging, overcoding, negation codes, and search strategy construction. Intended to guide indexers and searchers to create precise and/or comprehensive chemical patent searches and to interpret indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and applicability restrictions of codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Related to the scope of applicability of a code are restrictions placed on the types of compounds that can be assigned a certain code. For example, each code can only be used with certain subheadings, which are based on compound type. Some codes can only be used for patents classified in specific Derwent Sections; for example, most codes in Part R: are only assigned to Section B (Pharmaceutical, Veterinary, Medical) patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the relevant code Parts and subheading definitions when selecting codes; do not apply codes outside their permitted subheadings or Derwent Sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority rules when multiple codes apply
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of some codes is governed by priority rules that determine which code is used when there are several apparently 'correct' alternatives. Example: the priority rule for functional group codes states that Part K: should be consulted first, followed by Part L:, Part H:, and finally Part J:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply higher-priority Parts first; a correct code in a lower-priority part (e.g., Part J:) may be superseded and therefore not assigned if a higher-priority code applies. Example priority for ethers: only the highest priority ether attachment is coded in order heterocyclic > aromatic > alicyclic > aliphatic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set/Subset first-code priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The priority rule of many Sets and Subsets states that only the first correct code in that Set or Subset is assigned; other equally correct codes in that Set or Subset are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scanning a Set/Subset, assign only the first applicable code (e.g., Set M4: basic group codes M411–M417). Read codes in the order listed to determine the correct (first) code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred structural form for coding (tautomer preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some coding rules pertain to the preferred form of a structure. For example, when keto-enol tautomerism is possible, the structure is coded in the keto form, unless the -OH group of the enol form is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring, e.g., benzene. The same rule is assigned to analogous thioxo-thiol compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chapter-specific tautomer rules and examples (see 'Tautomerism' section) to choose which tautomer to code; preferred forms for classes (e.g., dyestuffs) are listed elsewhere in the manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polymers — use of special polymer codes and monomer handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Polymers are most specifically indexed with special polymer codes (contact Derwent for details). Some Chemical Codes are also assigned to polymers. The hypothetical monomers of >C=C< addition polymers are assigned all applicable Chemical Codes (e.g., polyvinyl chloride patents are assigned codes for vinyl chloride). From 1981 forward, polymers other than addition polymers have been coded as if they were single compounds, meaning that monomers or condensants have not been coded individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For addition polymers, include monomer codes; for non-addition polymers (post-1981) treat polymer as a single compound and use Poly codes to indicate repeating presence. From 1981, assign relevant negation and M1/M2/M3 Sets to polymers as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halogen coding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The code Part(s) used for coding a halogen-containing group depend on the atom(s) to which the halogen is bonded. The halogen atom itself is identified either in Set C0: or Subset H60:, depending on the atom(s) to which it is bonded. The functional group formed with the halogen may receive further codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the list of halogen fragments and the indicated code Parts/Sets (e.g., C0:, H6:, L-series codes) to select applicable codes; note historical identification conventions (X/Y placeholders and when particular halogen identification began).

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable substituents — include by OR'ing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Variable substituents can be included in Chemical Code searches by 'OR'ing together the codes applicable to the possible substituents. Varying substituents may affect related codes, which must also be OR'ed together as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh increased complexity vs. relevance gain before OR'ing many alternatives. Alternatives: delete highly variable portions for simplicity (less-specific search) or use Markush TOPFRAG to accept variable substituents and auto-create a strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unknown substituents — modify or delete counting codes
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are unknown substituents, all counting codes (codes that indicate the number of times a certain group is present) must be modified or deleted to take the unknown substituents into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OR together codes for all possible counts when a substituent could affect counts. Do not use negation codes when there are unknown substituents in the search structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness vs. relevance tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: As codes are being chosen, the user must decide how comprehensive the search is to be — i.e., which applicable codes, if any, should be omitted. Less restrictive strategies are more comprehensive but often retrieve many irrelevant answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance breadth vs. noise. Use other indexing terms (keywords, Manual Codes, company names) to restrict results and increase relevance, recognizing that narrowing may exclude pertinent references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use LINK operator rather than AND for code grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: The LINK operator is used for Chemical Code searching instead of the AND operator; LINK requires that all matching codes be located within the same code subfield. This ensures only codes related to a single chemical invention are matched, rather than codes anywhere in the same patent record causing a retrieval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link codes that must co-occur in the same invention subfield with LINK. Avoid a single AND of all selected codes across the record (not recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation codes — use to remove unwanted-ubiquitous fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: Negation codes were created to eliminate patents in which every structure disclosed has a particular fragment not wanted by the user. Negation codes are discussed in detail elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include negation codes in search statements to remove false drops caused by overcoding; remember indexers assign negation codes as 'essential codes' when all compounds in a subfield have the feature (inverse perspective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-ranging and use of time-range codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical Codes have changed over time; groups of codes introduced at the same time are associated with color/time ranges. Use time-range codes (M900–M903) to limit searches to patents indexed in particular periods and integrate multiple time-period searches via a time-ranging search statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct separate searches or a combined time-ranged statement so each distinct period uses the most specific codes available for that period (BLACK/RED/BLUE/GREEN mapping to M900–M903). Failure to time-range will bias retrieval toward records using newer codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadings (M0–M6) — restrict code searching to relevant subsets
rubrics_metrics.description: The CPI is divided into subsets labelled M0 through M6 (year- and subject-oriented). Subheadings are field labels limiting code searches to certain database subsets. The subheading(s) used depend on the type of structure being searched and the years relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer as few subheadings as possible for efficiency; include only those subheadings appropriate to the structure (e.g., M5 for cyclopenta(a)phenanthrene systems; M6 for apparatus/formulations). For polymers/natural products, use M0 for black codes and M1 for others as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard Chemical Code search strategy components
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard strategy typically comprises: Subheadings (field labels), Chemical Codes, Time range codes, the LINK operator, Negation codes, and Ring Index Numbers (RIN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct multi-statement searches that group codes by time-range and subset, LINK within statements, combine time-range statements appropriately, and apply negation codes to remove undesired hits. Example strategy shown in manual (S1..S7 with time-ranging and negation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Card records / code subfields reflect distinct chemical inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes corresponding to different chemical inventions within each patent are listed in different database subfields (formerly card records). Indexing lists codes for variable fragments together in the same subfield representing one invention; different inventions are on different subfields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When searching, LINK ensures matches within a single subfield (*01*, *02*, etc.). Be aware of the limits on how many alternatives can be coded in one subfield — overcoding can cause false drops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcoding rules (limits to combining alternatives in one subfield)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limits to the variety of compounds that can be coded in one card record (overcoding rules). Specific rules: compounds coded under different subheadings are never overcoded; compounds with 'polyvalent chain absent' (M320) should not be overcoded with those having 'polyvalent chain present' (M321–M323); compounds with/without functional groups in Parts H–L should not be overcoded together; compounds with different Basic Group codes (M411–M416) should not be overcoded. Since 1981, catalysts are coded in a separate subfield and always coded Q421.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow overcoding rules to reduce irrelevant hits from grouping too many alternatives; expect these rules to affect which codes appear together in a single subfield and thus how LINKed searches behave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning compounds to be coded — what Derwent indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Derwent indexes the widest chemical disclosure of patents (greatest range of compounds the patent can exclude others from making/using/selling). Types indexed include: all compounds and reaction intermediates stated to be new; products of new processes; new uses of known materials; detection media (since 1970, Sections B/C); materials recovered/purified in new ways; materials removed/removing agents (since 1977); activities/properties/uses; essential components of compositions; chemical formulations and apparatus; novel catalysts (since 1970); novel starting materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-essential known-function components are usually not structure-coded (e.g., a standard propellant), but may be searchable via Registry numbers or Manual Codes; in Sections B/C non-essential components may be structure-coded if they justify classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigning index terms other than Chemical Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before Chemical Codes are assigned, patents are entered with uncontrolled keywords, IPCs, bibliographic data, Manual Codes, and abstract words. These can be used for retrieval when non-structural information suffices or to refine Chemical Code search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine Chemical Code searches with Manual Codes or keywords (e.g., AND) to increase relevance; use Derwent Online tools and manuals to access these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derwent Registry numbers for common compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1981 a list of ~2100 commonly mentioned compounds/elements was assigned Registry numbers. A patent is indexed with a Registry number when it mentions a Registry compound as a significant compound or non-metallic element in the claims or examples (insignificant mentions such as generic solvents are excluded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Registry numbers to improve retrieval of frequently-occurring compounds; consult the CPI Registry Compounds User Guide for lists and synonyms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexer practice: err on side of comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical Codes are assigned to patents according to the same rules used for searching. Indexers tend to include extra codes, making it more likely that relevant patents will be retrieved. Because of the nature of patent searches, the choice is often made to err on the side of comprehensiveness rather than on the side of greater relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect indexer-included extra codes; when constructing searches, account for potential over-inclusion and use negation/manual codes/time-ranging to focus results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms, symbols, and reading order conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: One-character element symbols (T,U,V,W,X,Y,Z) are used as shorthand and have specified meanings. Some codes/symbols may appear similar but have different meanings (e.g., M1 vs M1: vs M1 as subheading vs negation). Phrases 'additionally coded'/'also coded' mean multiple Sets/Subsets are used. Punctuation ';' and ',' separate equally applicable code definitions. 'Other' covers remaining possibilities. Major coding changes occurred in 1981 and 'From 1981 forward' should be read as 'From 1981/Derwent Week 27 forward.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult chapter-specific notes for symbol meanings; read code lists in order for correct interpretation; be cautious interpreting similarly-looking codes in different contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush vs Chemical coding — coexistence and transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Markush coding (Derwent World Patents Index Markush) is a more recent indexing approach used with Markush DARC software. Although chemical indexing and Markush coding are being performed concurrently, chemical coding will probably be discontinued in the future; many older documents and the time lag mean Chemical Codes remain essential for comprehensive searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comprehensive historical searching is needed, include Chemical Codes (and time-range considerations) as many legacy records rely on them; be aware of the transition and use Markush tools when available for newer indexing.
